2b614a39a2.q: What percentage of AI investments show measurable ROI impact on company P&L according to recent studies?
2b614a39a2.a: According to a McKinsey study of 1,700 companies, only 6 percent are making real money on AI. Of that 6 percent, 72 percent were successful because they redesigned how the work gets done. Most AI investments today show up nowhere on the P&L, meaning companies cannot prove that a dollar invested created measurable returns.

5cda27ca91.q: What is the 'Olympian worker' concept and how does it relate to AI automation in the workplace?
5cda27ca91.a: The Olympian worker concept describes how AI automation removes busy work and administrative tasks, requiring employees to perform at a much higher cognitive level consistently. Just as only a few people can run a 100-meter dash in 10 seconds, not all workers will be able to adjust to having less busy work and more high cognitive work. Those who love their work will thrive, but those who just want routine tasks may struggle with this shift toward higher performance and continuous excellence.

2acab1449b.q: What is 'paving the cow path' and why is it a common mistake in AI implementation?
2acab1449b.a: Paving the cow path refers to automating existing broken processes rather than redesigning work from first principles. When an insurance benefits broker wanted AI to create the same manual spreadsheets their staff had always used, Genient instead showed them those spreadsheets were no longer needed. AI could automatically analyze data and triage next best actions, eliminating the need for four hours of manual work. The mistake is asking clients what they want rather than observing what they actually do and reimagining the process entirely.

094cc8d683.q: What does Genient mean by 'behavior-first operating model' in AI transformation?
094cc8d683.a: Behavior-first operating model means conducting qualitative research to understand actual processes through observation, rather than creating McKinsey-style swim lane diagrams or asking departments what they want. By observing broken processes, teams inspire new models that differ from what quantitative analysis alone would produce. This approach generates evangelism and optimism as people see themselves in the new operating model, with improved roles, careers, jobs, and compensation.
